Why measure first

The evidence says: AI amplifies what is already there

Four findings that shape how we work. None of them says AI does not work. All of them say the result depends on the foundations, and on measuring instead of assuming.

Amplifier

AI magnifies your existing practice [1]

The 2025 DORA report on AI-assisted software development concludes that AI's primary role is that of an amplifier: strong practices get stronger, and weak ones get exposed.

19%

Feeling faster is not being faster [2]

In a randomised trial of 16 experienced open-source developers on 246 real tasks, using AI tools made them 19% slower. They expected a 24% speed-up and still believed they had been about 20% faster afterwards. The authors stress that this is early-2025 tools in one setting.

+20%

Context files are not free [3]

An ETH Zurich study reported in March 2026 found that machine-generated agent context files lowered coding-agent success by about 3% while raising inference cost by over 20%. Developer-written files helped only slightly (about 4%). What you write, and how short you keep it, matters.

2027

The rules are moving; the expectation is not [4]

The EU's 2026 AI omnibus moved the high-risk obligations of the AI Act to 2 December 2027 (stand-alone systems) and 2 August 2028 (AI inside regulated products). The dates slipped. The expectation that you can show what AI you run and how you control it did not.

How we work

Four habits that run through every engagement

Check, don't trust

Every deliverable says how to verify it yourself. If we cannot say how, we do not claim it.

Measure before and after

We set the baseline first. Without one, a result is an anecdote.

Your team keeps the skill

We write things down, teach the method and hand over the tools. You should need us less each month.

Plain formats

Markdown, open standards and tests that run in your pipeline. Nothing locks you in.

Free self-check

Check where you stand in five minutes

Three short assessments. Each answer describes something observable, so you can pick what is true today instead of what you hope is true. Scores are worked out in your browser: nothing is sent or stored anywhere else unless you choose to share it.

Loading the assessments…

In Cisco's first AI Readiness Index (2023), 14% of 8,161 organisations surveyed were fully ready across six pillars: strategy, infrastructure, data, talent, governance and culture. Self-assessments tend to run optimistic, so when two answers seem to fit, choose the lower one. [5]

A self-assessment shows you where to look. An evidence-based review confirms what you find.
